newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss reinsurers' premiums fell 14.4 pct in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Swiss reinsurers' premiums fell 14.4 pct in 1995.

text.p: Swiss reinsurance companies' combined premium income fell 14.4 percent in 1995 from 1994 levels, weighed down by the strong Swiss franc's effect on exchange rates, the Federal Office for Private Insurers said.

A drop in foreign business contributed around six percent of the total decline, which was far worse than the 4.3 percent drop in total premiums recorded in 1994, the office said. It did not give any absolute figures.

The strong franc also hurt accident and property insurers, whose premium income dipped 1.8 percent after rising 1.6 percent in 1994. Their Swiss premiums rose 1.8 percent, off from the three percent growth seen in 1994.
Life insurers' business rose six percent, slower than the 10.5 percent growth in 1994. Their premium income in Switzerland rose 14.3 percent, up from 11.4 percent.
"In all the Swiss direct insurance business continued to develop positively, rising 9.3 percent versus 8.2 percent the year earlier," it said in a statement.
The report was based on 128 Swiss insurance companies under the office's aegis. It does not include around 70 health insurance funds that won approval this year to offer extra private insurance.

It said Switzerland and Liechtenstein were close to concluding an insurance agreement that should reduce the disadvantages Swiss insurers have faced since Liechtenstein joined the European Economic Area in May.
Until then, business in Liechtenstein had counted as domestic business for Swiss companies.
